newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - Lufthansa results hit by fuel costs.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Lufthansa results hit by fuel costs.

text.p: Deutsche Lufthansa AG said on Thursday profits for the first nine months of the year fell largely as a result of surging fuel costs, adding it expected full-year profits to be at best 10 percent down on 1995.
But Lufthansa said if its previously announced cost-cutting scheme went according to plan it would be in line for a significant improvement in profits for 1997.

Lufthansa, preparing for the final stage of its privatisation starting later this year, said pre-tax profits for the first three-quarters fell to 434 million marks ($285 million) compared to 506 million in the same period a year-ago.
The figures were slightly below analyst expectations, most of which ranged between 440 and 460 million marks.

Chief executive Juergen Weber said a 18 percent jump in fuel expenses, costing the carrier an extra 193 million marks in the period, was the main factor behind the fall and said the airline was determined to further reduce its overall costs.
"Our goal is to reduce unit costs by 20 percent by the year 2000," Weber told a news briefing.
The airline also said results were dragged down by losses in its cargo business, which was not expected to make a profit until 1998.
In the first nine months, Lufthansa airlines carried some 31.3 million passengers, a gain of 1.4 percent, and the carrier said traffic data for the fourth quarter had so far been "favourable".
But finance chief Klaus Schlede added that fourth quarter profits were unlikely to improve upon the 250 million mark pre-tax figure recorded a year ago.
"We expect in the best case that profits for this year will be 10 percent below those last year."
He added that if the airline managed to reduce its costs as planned, 1998 could however bring "a significant improvement" in its profits. "But planning is always ambitious," he added.
Shares in Frankfurt-listed Lufthansa initially fell after the results but later came back to trade just 10 pfennigs higher at 19.85 marks in a firmer overall market.

Lufthansa said that profits for the last quarter depended largely on the outcome of a continuing pay dispute with workers which has already led to brief stoppages earlier this month and cost the firm 10 million marks in lost earnings.
The German airline is facing strong price-competition in its domestic market from foreign rivals and has been accused of charging too much on national flights.
But Weber said the airline was becoming more flexible in its pricing and special offers and had made service improvements that now put it among the most consistently punctual airlines in Europe.
"We know that the German market is particularly attractive and that Lufthansa is particularly affected and challenged as a result," Weber said.
Outside fuel costs, the other main drag on the results was a 66 million loss made by its cargo business, compared to a 12 million profit in the first three quarters of last year. ($1=1.5255 Mark)
